info.text:
The other country doesn't pay the tariff. So who does?

The US importer pays the tariff to US Customs at the border.
Our own example: $100 of acorns + a 10% tariff = $10 owed, $110 landed cost. The importer can raise prices, absorb it, or split it.
Research on the 2018 tariffs (Amiti, Redding and Weinstein, 2019) found nearly full pass-through to US import prices; a New York Fed study (Feb 2026) estimated US firms and consumers bore nearly 90% of 2025 tariffs. A 2021 study found store prices rose less, as retailers absorbed some.
US customs duties: $77.0 billion in fiscal 2024, $194.9 billion in fiscal 2025 (Treasury).

Sources: Journal of Economic Perspectives (2019); Federal Reserve Bank of New York (Feb 2026); Cavallo et al., AER: Insights (2021); US Treasury; example math by FinancePros TV.
News and education, not financial advice.
